verdict.rationale: Cloudflare's MoQ relay is itself a relay. It organizes media into namespaces and tracks, and clients connect with subscribe-scoped tokens, so publish/subscribe routing through the relay is documented. The docs never explicitly state that each subscriber receives only the specific tracks it subscribes to; that per-track selective forwarding is only implied by the MoQ track model. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of per-track selective subscription and forwarding, details on fan-out behavior per participant, and independent hands-on corroboration of selective track delivery.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, media routes through a selective forwarding unit or relay that delivers only the tracks each participant subscribes to

citations.quote: Each relay provides an isolated scope — your namespaces, tracks, and objects are separated from those belonging to other relays.
You control who can publish and who can subscribe by issuing tokens scoped to the operations each client needs.
Cloudflare returns a relay ID and two default tokens: one that can publish and subscribe, and one that can only subscribe.
It provides efficient, low-latency media streaming by leveraging QUIC's multiplexing and connection management capabilities.
